items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We met an American white couple... The fellow was Sid Tracey... We took photographs posing with camels... We posed with shark teeth and with the natives.

ctx.x: After we left Port Tewfik I noticed quite a number of Arabic people on the lower deck of the ship with what must have been their worldly belongings. Leon, who had made a trip like this before, told me that they were deck passengers. This deck was covered with a canvas cover to protect the passengers from the sun and at night the weather was very warm, so these people who could not afford to travel even in third class cabins, slept on the deck at night, eat in the third class dining rooms and spent the days on the…

We met an American white couple who were dancers that were also going to Bombay to work at the Taj Mahal. They were known as Tracey and Hay. The fellow was Sid Tracey and the woman was Bessie Hay. The 28th of October we arrived in Aden, Arabia and went ashore with Hay and Tracey. We took photographs posing with camels that didn't have a life that was easy like those in the zoos. These camels had to work. We posed with shark teeth and with the natives. We had stopped the day before at Massawa which was Italian…

The whole voyage was wonderful and I felt as though I was living in wonderland. We arrived at Bombay the 2nd of November, ten sailing days from Venice. We were met by the manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel who was a Mr. Faletti, an Italian who was a naturalised English citizen, and two Negro musicians who were living in India and were going to play with the Abbey band. One was Cricket Smith, a trumpet player and the other was Rudy Jackson, an alto sax man. Cricket and Rudy had come to Europe in the early 20s.
